What this means for your business

The goal is not to accuse someone. It is to make sure the business controls its domain, hosting, accounts, code, content, data, invoices, and current work if the relationship ends.

What to watch

  • The business cannot log in to the domain or hosting.
  • Progress exists only in screenshots or promises.
  • Dates move without a written new plan.
  • No backup, project files, export, or handoff instructions.

Do this next

  1. Save the contract, invoices, messages, and latest working links.
  2. Confirm business-owned access to domain, hosting, visit tracking, forms, email, and payment tools.
  3. Request a written status, deliverables, blockers, and handoff date.
  4. Get technical or legal help before deleting access or starting a dispute.

When Little Fight fits

We can inspect what exists and write a recovery map. We are not lawyers and will not diagnose intent from silence.

Get a plain-English second opinion

Sources and further reading

Product features and rules can change. Use the linked source as the current word.

insight.answer: Secure your business assets now if you see a pattern: missed written milestones, missing access, no working evidence, and no recovery plan. One slow reply on its own is not proof.
